title: The invention of the Internet
subtitle: Networks
subject: sciences
description: The Internet does not have a single inventor. It's a long chain: a military network, a common language, then the Web for humans.

hero.hook: First a network to resist the war. Then the whole world tunes in.

blocks.text: The Internet was not born from a single genius in a garage. It is a collective construction over several decades.
Three simple steps to remember: a first network (ARPANET), a common language (TCP/IP), then an easy interface (the Web).

At the end of the **1960** years, in the midst of the Cold War, the American army financed a project: connecting computers so that they continued to communicate even if part of the network was destroyed.

blocks.caption: ARPANET first connects a few American universities.

blocks.text: This network is called **ARPANET**. Messages are split into small packets which take different paths. If one road falls, another takes over.

For different networks to understand each other, common rules are needed. **Vint Cerf** and **Bob Kahn** are developing the **TCP/IP** protocol: a language that tells how to cut, address and recompose data.

blocks.caption: Cerf and Kahn: the architects of the language of the Internet.

blocks.text: On January 1 **1983**, ARPANET officially switched to TCP/IP. Many consider this date to be the technical “birth” of the Internet.

sections.title: The Web makes the network human

blocks.text: The Internet is the network. The **World Wide Web**, invented by **Tim Berners-Lee** at CERN at the beginning of the years **1990**, is the easy layer: pages, links, browsers.
Without the Web, the Internet would remain primarily a tool for experts. With it, everyone can click.

sections.title: The nervous system of the world

blocks.text: Today, the Internet carries emails, videos, banks, hospitals, GPS. It has also created new problems: disinformation, surveillance, digital divide.
The Internet was born from ARPANET, became universal thanks to TCP/IP, and accessible thanks to the Web. This is not a unique invention, it is a shared architecture.
